Carla: Heads-up — saw a perf regression in canary after enabling the hybrid per-layer int4+fp8 strategy. We excluded embeddings & lm_head as usual, but overall latency is ~12% higher on short sequences (<256). Kernel selector keeps flipping between int4 and fp8 on mid layers, looks like a thrash. Attaching a tiny profiler snippet below.

Ben: Can you paste the profiler output and the canary config? CPU vs GPU breakdown?

Carla: pasted snippet:
```
KernelSwitch: layer 9 -> fp8  (setup=3.2ms)
KernelSwitch: layer 10 -> int4 (setup=4.1ms)
KVCache: hit_rate=0.88
BatchSize distribution: [1,1,2,1,1]
Throughput: 820 tok/s (baseline) -> 720 tok/s (hybrid)
```

Alice: small/imbalanced batches + partially cold KV cache will amplify kernel-switch overhead. Selector hysteresis looks low for these workloads. Also dynamic per-batch calibration can invalidate cached kernels frequently.

Dan: ran microbench (same model) to double-check on A100 cluster: 
- baseline int8-only: 940 tok/s
- hybrid (per-layer int4 + fp8 fallback): 760 tok/s
- force fp8 on identified "sensitive" layers only: 900 tok/s
- disable selector hysteresis: 730 tok/s (worse)

Erin: Proposal: increase kernel selector stickiness (stickiness_ms) from 50 -> 250, and add a batch-size threshold so that when effective batch < 4 we prefer the current kernel unless a big perf delta is expected. Also short-circuit kernel probes if KV hit ratio > 0.6.

Frank: Seen something similar — our calibration flow was doing per-batch dynamic scaling for fp8 and that caused lots of kernel cache churn. If we do calibration offline (deployment-time) the kernels stay stable and perf improves.

deploy-bot: canary deploy 2025-11-08T09:12 applied; traffic=5% :rocket:

Carla: Action items: (1) bump selector hysteresis & add batch-threshold (Erin?), (2) change calibration to offline per-layer as default (Alice?), (3) add a micro-repro/perf test for kernel-switch cost (Dan?), (4) add a kv-warmup option for canary to increase initial KV hit rate (Ben?). Who volunteers to own?

Ben: I'll pick up (4) and wire a quick kv-warmup flag on the canary path. Will also add a tiny script to cold-start with 100 short seqs.

Alice: I'll prototype offline calibration flow and run microbench with static per-layer scales. Expect to push a branch by EOD tomorrow.

Dan: I'll add a perf regression test that injects skewed batch-size distributions and measures kernel-switch overhead / throughput delta.

Erin: I'll update the selector config defaults (stickiness_ms + batch-threshold) and open a PR with rationale and perf numbers.

Frank: I'll document the dynamic-calibration caveat in the quantization README and add a warning in the canary checklist.

Carla: Thanks — I'll collect the logs and post a reproducer gist. If we converge on these changes we can re-run canary at 25% with kv-warmup and offline calibration.

Ben: sounds good. I'll also add a quick perf dashboard card for kernel-switch events so we can track regressions automatically. :+1:

Carla: awesome — ping me on the PRs and i'll triage.
